data.title: Navitas Semiconductor Acquires Patent Portfolio for $5 Million Upfront Plus Royalties
data.description:
Navitas Semiconductor USA entered into a patent assignment agreement to acquire patents and patent applications from Longitude Flash Memory Solutions and Longitude Licensing. The deal requires a $5 million upfront payment, a potential additional $5 million upon specified litigation outcomes, and a 1.5% share of gross revenue from monetizing the patents; the assignors also terminated related intercompany licenses and agreements.

data.title: BioNexus Gene Lab Authorizes Share Repurchase Program of Up to $2 Million
data.description:
BioNexus Gene Lab authorized a share repurchase program with a spending limit of $2 million for up to 12 months.

Key Highlights:

  • The program allows open-market repurchases through November 23, 2027, unless the limit is reached or the program ends earlier.
  • Purchases will be funded with existing unrestricted corporate cash; the $2 million cap includes transaction costs and any applicable excise tax reserve.
  • Repurchases are discretionary and will depend on market conditions, cash availability, capital needs and legal and Nasdaq listing requirements.
  • The company will set a share limit before trading to maintain a cushion above Nasdaq public float and public holder requirements.
  • Repurchased shares will become authorized but unissued; any later issuance requires separate Board approval and other applicable approvals.

Original SEC Filing: BioNexus Gene Lab Corp [ BGLC ] - 8-K - Nov. 27, 2026

data.title: U.S. Corn, Wheat Export Sales Rose Last Week
data.description:
By Anthony Harrup

U.S. corn and wheat export sales came in above expectations last week, while soybean export sales fell by half from the week before, according to the Department of Agriculture's latest report.

Corn export sales for the 2026-2027 marketing year totaled 1.93 million metric tons in the week ended Nov. 19, up 21% from the week before, the USDA said on Friday. Wheat sales for 2026-2027 rose 64% to 564,700 tons.

Soybean sales fell 50% to 755,800 tons for 2026-2027 while 2,200 tons of soybeans were sold to Japan for the 2027-2028 marketing year.

Analyst estimates in a Wall Street Journal survey ranged from 250,000 tons to 550,000 tons for wheat, from 700,000 tons to 1.77 million tons for corn, and from 800,000 tons to 1.6 million tons for soybeans.

Mexico was the main buyer of corn and soybeans last week, while wheat sales were mainly to unknown destinations and Mexico.

To see related data, search "U.S. Export Sales: Weekly Sales Totals" in Dow Jones NewsPlus.

Write to Anthony Harrup at anthony.harrup@wsj.com

data.title: Steady to firm prices expected heading into the weekend
data.description:
The following are expectations for the resumption of grain and soy complex trading at the Chicago Board of Trade at 8:30 a.m. CST (1430 GMT) on Friday.

The markets will have an abbreviated trading session after closing on Thursday for the US Thanksgiving holiday.

WHEAT - Up 2 to 4 cents per bushel

  • CBOT wheat was expected to rise due to firm EU prices and short covering ahead of the weekend, analysts said.

  • Euronext wheat prices climbed to one-month highs on ongoing war disruptions to Black Sea trade.

  • Russia attacked two foreign cargo ships carrying more than 100,000 metric tons of grain near Ukraine's Black Sea port of Odesa, Ukrainian Prime Minister Sergiy Koretskyi said on Thursday.

  • Consultancy SovEcon raised its forecast for Russia's 2026 wheat crop by 0.4 million metric tons to 88.5 million metric tons on Friday.

  • US wheat export sales for 2026-27 were 564,700 metric tons in the week that ended on November 19, the US Department of Agriculture said. This exceeded analysts' expectations of 250,000 to 550,000 metric tons.

  • Rain in the Midwest was benefiting US soft red winter wheat crops, Commodity Weather Group said.

  • On Wednesday, CBOT March soft red winter wheat ended down 1-3/4 cents at $5.87-1/2 per bushel after earlier touching the lowest level for a most-active contract since June 30.

CORN - Steady to up 2 cents per bushel

  • Weekly US corn export sales for 2026-27 were 1.9 million metric tons, the USDA said. Analysts expected 700,000 to 2 million metric tons.

  • Actively traded CBOT March corn fell to a five-month low last week and matched that low on Tuesday. Prices have retreated sharply from a three-year high reached in September.

  • Outside markets looked supportive, analysts said, with oil prices were set to snap a three-week losing streak.

  • On Wednesday, CBOT March corn ended 6-1/4 cents higher to $4.56-1/2 a bushel.

SOYBEANS - Up 1 to 3 cents per bushel

  • CBOT soybeans were expected to rise as traders monitor crop weather in South America.

  • Consultancy Agroconsult on Thursday pegged Brazil's 2026-27 soybean crop at 182.3 million metric tons, down 1.3% from the previous season. The firm still projected record-large exports in 2027.

  • Argentina's soybean planting for the 2026-27 cycle was 39.7% complete, while corn planting reached 52.7%, the Buenos Aires grains exchange said on Thursday.

  • Weekly US soybean export sales for 2026-27 were 755,800 metric tons, below analysts' estimates of 800,000 to 2 million metric tons.

  • On Wednesday, CBOT January soybeans finished 10 cents higher at $12.44 a bushel.

data.title: SAP source code target of cyberattack; company says no customer data compromised: report
data.description:
Hackers, possibly using AI-assisted tools, were able to target SAP's source code stored on GitHub, according to Der Spiegel, which said the German-based enterprise software firm had confirmed the attack.

Once SAP identified suspicious activity within GitHub, the company immediately took action to mitigate the attack and protect its customers and services, according to the report. The hackers had gained access by acquiring employee authentication tokens, which allowed them to copy and alter source code in GitHub.

"Based on our investigation to date, we have found no evidence of unauthorized access to customer business data," SAP said, according to SecurityWeek.

There was also no evidence of tampered code being delivered to SAP's clients. Some of the protective measures included the replacement of signing keys, limited access to GitHub and a suspension of automated development operations.

Seeking Alpha reached out to SAP for comment.

There has been a clear increase in cyberattacks across businesses, government agencies and critical infrastructure. It was reported on Friday that hackers breached the US Air Force's flagship cloud computing platform in a development that could jeopardize sensitive tactical, personnel and logistics data.

data.title: Svatantra Microfin gets SEBI nod to proceed with ₹3,000 crore IPO
data.description:
Svatantra Microfin Ltd, the non-banking financial company led by Ananya Birla, has received observations from the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) for its proposed initial public offering (IPO). Besides, seven other companies — Sterlite Electric Ltd, Gaurik Fashions Ltd, Emerald Jewel Industry India Ltd, Beauty Garage Ltd, Noble Hygiene Ltd, MP Steel (India) Ltd and Kataria Dhulchand Pannalal Jewellers Ltd — have also received approval from the market regulator.

The Svatantra Microfin issue totals ₹3,000 crore, split equally between a fresh issue of ₹1,500 crore and an offer for sale of ₹1,500 crore. The company plans to use the fresh issue proceeds to strengthen its Tier I capital base and meet future requirements, including onward lending linked to business growth. The equity shares are proposed to be listed on BSE and the NSE.

Axis Capital, Avendus Capital, IIFL Capital Services, Kotak Mahindra Capital Company and SBI Capital Markets are the book running lead managers.

Ananya Birla is Chairperson and Non-Executive Director of the company. It was the first institution to receive an NBFC-MFI licence, introduced by the Reserve Bank of India in 2011.

As of March 31, 2026, Svatantra Microfin was the second-largest NBFC-MFI in India by microfinance assets under management (AUM). Its AUM grew at a compounded annual rate of 20.87 per cent, from ₹14,437.87 crore in March 2024 to ₹21,093.22 crore in March 2026. Its market share rose from 3.26 per cent to 6.37 per cent in the period.

The company reported a Gross Stage 3 ratio of 1.19 per cent in Fiscal 2026, the lowest among its microfinance peers. Its return on equity stood at 15.00 per cent.

It operates 2,123 branches across 20 States and 394 districts, with 24,594 employees. It served 4,266,316 active borrowers as of March 31, 2026. Chaitanya India Fin Credit Private Ltd was merged into the company effective March 21, 2026.

Meanwhile, Bvishal Oil and Energy Ltd and Pentacle Consultants (I) Ltd withdrew their draft offer documents.

data.title: Adani group seeks government nod to invest in India’s airline sector
data.description:
The diversified Adani group, which runs multiple airports across the country, has requested the government to allow it to invest in the airline sector, a top official said on Friday.

Group chief finance officer Jugeshinder Robbie Singh told reporters that over 60 crore people in the country can fly, and the number of daily flights needs to go up by nearly 10 times to 30,000.

Adani group seeks government nod for airline investments

“And that’s why we requested the government to at least allow us to invest, so that we can facilitate the development of airlines. Some fund, some other airline company and things like that...or an entrepreneur who wants to go into that space,” the CFO said while speaking on the sidelines of the India Debt Capital Market Summit here.

In July this year, the group said it was “not evaluating any proposal to enter the airlines business”. On November 3, Adani Airport Holdings chief executive Arun Bansal had ruled out entering the airlines business, saying that it is never a good strategy to compete with customers.

Group operates eight airports handling over one-fourth of passenger traffic

Adani group runs eight airports in the country, including the ones in the financial capital and the satellite city of Navi Mumbai, and also Ahmedabad, Lucknow and Guwahati, which ferry over one-fourth of the country’s air passenger traffic.

Airline sector remains a virtual duopoly

The airline business has been reduced to a virtual duopoly with two strong domestic carriers -- the Tata Group-led Air India and Rahul Bhatia-run IndiGo, ruling the skies with a 90 per cent market share.

Problems at IndiGo last year, which led to thousands of flight cancellations, led to voices demanding more airlines to operate in the country.

data.title: BMW targets 20,000 plus sales in 2026, MINI volumes seen doubling
data.description:
BMW Group India is aiming to cross 20,000 passenger vehicle sales in 2026 and nearly double MINI volumes to 1,200-1,400 units as it expands its EV portfolio and rolls out new products, even as the luxury carmaker prepares to raise prices by 2-4 per cent across its range from January 2027.

Speaking after the launch of the new all-electric MINI Cooper SE and the limited-run Paul Smith Editions, BMW Group India President and CEO Hardeep Singh Brar said the company has already crossed 1,000 MINI sales this year, compared with annual volumes of 700-800 units over the past five years. MINI had retailed 730 units in 2025.

“December is always a strong month, contributing 10-12 per cent of annual sales. Depending on year-end demand, MINI could post growth of 70-100 per cent this year,” Brar said.

Currency pressure

BMW expects another busy December as customers rush to buy ahead of the planned price increase. The company has cited currency pressures, particularly the rupee’s depreciation against the euro, as a key reason for the revision.

Brar said BMW continues to absorb part of the impact despite implementing cumulative price hikes of 8-9 per cent since last year. “We are still under-recovering by around 10 per cent because of exchange-rate movements,” he noted.

The company launched four MINI models, including the second-generation Cooper SE electric hatchback priced at ₹53.9 lakh. Powered by a 54.2 kWh battery pack, the model offers a claimed WLTP range of 402 km and deliveries will begin in December.

Lower import duties under the India-UK free trade agreement have enabled BMW to price imported MINI models closer to the locally assembled Countryman, reducing the immediate need for local production of niche hatchbacks, Brar said.

EV adoption

On electrification, BMW expects EVs to account for around 30 per cent of its India sales next year, up from about 26 per cent currently. Brar ruled out introducing plug-in hybrids, saying growing EV adoption and upcoming models with ranges exceeding 700 km make them unnecessary.

The sales push comes amid an intensifying battle with Mercedes-Benz for leadership of India’s luxury car market. BMW currently leads retail registrations and expects to retain the top position through 2026. Several key models, including the iX1, i5, 5 Series, 7 Series and i7, are carrying waiting periods of two to three months.

The company is also seeing strong demand for personalisation, with around 40 per cent of MINI buyers opting for customisation packages, while markets such as Keralam, Punjab and Hyderabad are emerging as important growth centres.

data.title: Portugal's TAP Q3 profit halves as soaring jet fuel costs bite
data.description:
Portuguese flag carrier TAP on Friday posted a 51.3% drop in third-quarter net profit to €61.3 million ($67.3 million), as a sharp rise in jet fuel costs offset higher passenger revenue.

  • TAP, in which Portugal's government is selling a stake of up to 49.9% to Germany's Lufthansa , said revenue increased 1.8% to €1.35 billion, with passenger revenue rising 3.6% to €1.24 billion

  • Passenger revenue per available seat kilometre grew 4.4%, with gains across all markets, led by Africa, where it rose 7%, followed by Europe, up 5%

  • However, earnings before interest and taxes fell 36.4% year-on-year to €126.2 million, as jet fuel costs surged 32.4% to €356 million

  • Chief Executive Luis Rodrigues said in a statement that the third quarter "confirmed the resilience of TAP's business model amid the significant impact of rising fuel prices"

  • "The commercial measures we have implemented started to deliver results during the quarter, particularly towards the end of the period, and we are entering the fourth quarter with stronger revenue momentum," he said

  • Passenger numbers fell 0.6% to 4.77 million in the quarter, while the load factor declined by 0.5 percentage points to 87.4%

($1 = 0.9107 euros)

data.title: Blue Gold and Current Technology Partner to Bring Agentic AI Payments to Blue Gold’s Gold-Powered Banking App
data.description:
Collaboration will let customers authorize AI agents to pay, transfer and settle in gold, positioning Blue Gold in a market forecast to reach nearly USD 400 billion by 2035

NEW YORK, Nov. 27, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Blue Gold Limited (Nasdaq: BGL, BGLWW) (“Blue Gold” or the “Company”) today announced that it has signed a Memorandum of Understanding with Current Technology (TripleBolt Technology Corporation) (“Current”), an AI-native software and consulting firm, to bring agentic AI payments into Blue Gold’s new gold-powered banking app. Under the collaboration, Blue Gold customers will be able to authorize AI agents to initiate and manage payments, bill pay, transfers and purchases on their behalf, within spending limits and permissions they set and can revoke at any time. Payments are expected to settle in gold or gold-backed balances where available, combining the stability of gold with the speed and convenience of AI-driven commerce.

According to Deloitte, by 2030, agentic commerce could drive up to $17.5 trillion in commerce, making it a pivotal force in the future of payments and consumer engagement.

The payments layer that powers this shift is growing quickly. According to DataM Intelligence, the global agentic payments market was valued at USD 18 million in 2025 and is projected to reach USD 398.99 billion by 2035, a compound annual growth rate of 172%. North America led the market with an estimated 36.8% share in 2025. Growth is driven by AI agents making autonomous purchases, new agentic commerce protocols and payment standards, and rising demand for frictionless, personalized checkout.

“The question isn’t whether agentic payments will transform financial services—it’s whether your organization will lead this transformation or be disrupted by it,” said Kevin Clark, Executive Chairman of Blue Gold. “The infrastructure is being built, the market is expanding rapidly, and early movers are already gaining competitive advantages.”

“Agentic payments are moving from concept to real money movement, and the institutions that build them in now will set the standard,” said Erin Barton, Co-Founder and Chief Operating Officer of Current. “Blue Gold has the gold infrastructure and a clear vision for modern banking. Our job is to deliver agents that customers can trust with their money: clear permissions, strong controls and a full audit trail behind every transaction. We are proud to help Blue Gold bring that to market.”

The collaboration is expected to cover agentic payment experience design, AI agent development, integration with Blue Gold’s banking and gold settlement infrastructure, support for emerging agentic commerce standards, and controls for consent, fraud prevention and compliance. The parties intend to begin with a pilot before a broader rollout.

data.title: Belgium Inflation Eases To 5.09% In November
data.description:
BRUSSELS/FRANKFURT/PARIS (dpa-AFX) - Belgium's consumer price inflation eased slightly in November from a 42-month high in the previous month, figures from the statistical office showed on Friday.

The consumer price index climbed 5.09 percent year-over-year in November, slower than the 5.26 percent rise in October, which was the highest inflation rate since April 2023.

Services inflation moderated to 4.12 percent from 4.73 percent, while the deflation in food prices, including alcoholic beverages, eased to 0.04 percent from 0.18 percent. The health cost index was 4.70 percent higher versus 4.53 percent in October

Inflation based on energy rose to 33.69 percent from 33.22 percent a month ago. Excluding energy products and unprocessed food, core inflation slowed to 2.47 percent from 2.8 percent in October.

On a monthly basis, consumer prices moved up 0.4 percent in November.

data.title: Washout holds, rebound emerges
data.description:
Key points:
  • US equity index futures rally: Nasdaq 100 up >2%
  • STOXX 600 index gains ~1%
  • Dollar gains; bitcoin, US crude both up ~1%; gold up >2%
  • US 10-year Treasury yield rises to ~4.90%

WASHOUT HOLDS, REBOUND EMERGES

A strong rebound is taking shape ahead of Friday's open as investors return from the Thanksgiving break and pile back into beaten-down AI and technology shares. US stock futures are sharply higher, with E-mini Nasdaq 100 futures up more than 2%, easily leading the advance.

From a technical perspective, Wednesday may have been more important than it first appeared. Both E-mini Nasdaq 100 futures and E-mini S&P 500 futures carved out bullish hammer candlesticks, a pattern that often emerges near market lows when buyers step in and reverse an earlier selloff.

The signal was especially notable because it developed as the major indexes, including the Nasdaq 100 , held above last week's panic lows. In other words, sellers failed to gain fresh downside traction, leaving the door open for a rebound.

That follow-through is emerging Friday morning. Nearly every S&P Select Sector SPDR fund is trading higher ahead of the bell, with 7 of the 11 sectors up more than 1%. Technology is the clear leader, gaining more than 2.5%, while consumer staples is the lone sector modestly in the red.

Elsewhere, regional banks are up about 0.8%, while chip stocks are among the market's standout performers. The PHLX Semiconductor ETF is jumping more than 4% as investors return to growth-oriented areas of the market.

Retailers are also getting a lift from holiday shopping expectations. Adobe forecasts a record $12.9 billion in online Black Friday spending this year, up 9.2% from a year ago. The S&P Retail ETF is up about 0.8% in premarket trading.

Investors should keep in mind that Friday's session is shortened, with US stock markets closing at 1 p.m. ET and bond markets at 2 p.m. ET. Historically, the post-Thanksgiving trading day is one of the lightest-volume sessions of the year, which can sometimes amplify market moves.

Here is a snapshot of where markets stood around 8:55 a.m. ET.

data.title: From squishies to can crushers: The toys on the top of Santa's list
data.description:
Forget about an official Red Ryder Carbine-Action 200-shot range model air rifle—the toys kids are waiting to unwrap this holiday season are squishy, loud, and, as always, pricey.

Compiling a list of the most popular toys depends on who you ask. Amazon and Target are probably the most popular destinations for kids under 10, while kids 10 and up would most likely prefer their parents shop at Best Buy for game consoles, laptops, earbuds, and, of course, the digital download code for Grand Theft Auto VI .

Doubling as both collectibles and a calming sensory tool, squishies—including dumpling squishies—are still at the top spot at both Amazon and Target . The tactile toys are made from slow-rising polyurethane foam that gives a satisfying squeeze and are available in almost unlimited shapes and sizes—from raindrop-shaped squishies to animal-shaped squishies to squishies shaped like a stick of butter.

For creative types, Stickerbox lets kids (and some adults) make their own stickers using AI to generate designs and is equipped with thermal printing that avoids costly ink refills. The $130 Stickerbox is designed to block inappropriate prompts to make sure each sticker is kid-friendly.

Expanding on its "dinosaur hatching" phenomenon from last year, Primal Hatch now allows kids to hatch their own megalodon. Put the egg in the tank, add water, and watch while a shark is “born.” Best part? The color-changing, explosive hatching action can be repeated over and over. Primal Hatch is available at Amazon , Walmart , and Target with Amazon offering the best price of $35.

Got a young recycler at home? The Crunchinator and ChompSaw let kids crush empty soda cans and cut up cardboard boxes instead of tossing them.

Designed by a NASA engineer, the $35 Crunchinator enables kids to crush and smash objects in what the company calls “the most satisfyingly destructive ways possible.”

To make use of all those empty Amazon boxes, the $130 Chompshop Chompsaw cuts old cardboard boxes into any shape and any creation to make dioramas, classroom projects, costumes, and whatever else kids can dream up.

For more mindless entertainment, there’s the flying orb ball toy, a “hand-controlled mini drone flight spinner” that can fly, hover, and even respond like a boomerang, all with RGB lighting that creates a mesmerizing light display.

Mattel is continuing to cash in on the KPop juggernaut with a new line of KPop Demon Hunters toys, while Disney is leaning on a holiday evergreen—a Toy Story figurine line featuring Woody, Jessie, Buzz, Slinky, Rex, and Forky in movie-inspired scale.

Electronics are still a favorite among teens, tweens, and adults with the Consumer Technology Association finding that at least 87% of adults plan to buy tech gifts this holiday season. The most popular for 2026 includes Apple AirPods 5, Sony cameras, and Ray-Ban Meta smart glasses, showing that the most-wanted gifts still come with a charging cable.

Target , Amazon , and Best Buy all have the Nintendo Switch 2 Console as one of its bestselling items this holiday season. The next generation of the Nintendo Switch comes with a $500 price tag but gives gamers three play modes: TV, tabletop, and handheld. While the console is compatible with all Nintendo Switch games, it still can’t get you to Vice City.

The toys might change every year—still squishy, still loud, and still pricey—but the mission never does: find the right one before someone else does.

data.title: BofA sets 2027 S&P 500 target at 7,800 after pullback
data.description:
Bank of America Securities this week introduced a 2027 year-end S&P 500 (SP500) target of 7,800, contending that a recent market pullback has created an attractive entry point despite looming earnings deceleration and supply-demand headwinds.

The forecast implies roughly 8.6% upside from Wednesday’s close of 7,182.86—and about 7% from Friday’s implied futures open of 7,290.94—with BofA’s underlying models mapping a wider potential range between 6,600 and 8,500. The index's all-time intraday high is 7,844.52, set in October.

Strategists remain constructive on the back of compressed price-to-earnings multiples and untapped AI-driven productivity gains, noting that higher capital costs and regulatory hurdles should prevent an AI capital expenditure overheat. Reflecting greater value for existing AI capacity, BofA upgraded communication services to Overweight while highlighting stronger conviction in AI adoption through Overweight ratings on financials and health care .

Still, BofA projects S&P 500 earnings-per-share growth to slow sharply from 35% ($370) in 2026 to 14% ($420) in 2027—modestly below the $428 consensus—before normalizing to 7% ($450) in 2028. Because chipmakers drive the bulk of profit growth, a 20% cut in AI spending could directly shave 8% off index EPS, compounding broader downside risks from rising equity issuance, waning share buybacks, and potential demographic-driven retirement outflows.

data.title: Brazil's Raizen explores sale of fuel distribution arm, shareholder says
data.description:
By Luciana Magalhaes

Brazilian energy and commodities company Raizen is considering the sale of its fuel distribution arm as part of a broader divestment plan, founding shareholder Rubens Ometto told Reuters on Friday.

Raizen is wrapping up a major restructuring to resolve roughly 65 billion reais ($11.7 billion) of debt, splitting into two independent entities after shareholders approved the separation of the company's fuel distribution and lubricants unit — to be known as Raizen SA — from Raizen Energia, which will contain the sugar, ethanol and bioenergy operations.

"It is one of the alternatives under consideration today," Ometto said, adding that while prospective buyers are already looking at the deal, no formal process is under way.

He declined to name potential suitors or disclose how much Raizen hopes to fetch from a sale.

Brazilian media have speculated that Abu Dhabi sovereign wealth fund Mubadala could be among the groups potentially interested in Raizen's distribution unit once a formal process begins, though the fund has declined to comment.

Ometto, whose conglomerate Cosan controls Raizen alongside joint venture partner Shell, said he has not yet decided whether to inject fresh capital into the company as part of a restructuring that would dilute his stake in the ethanol producer.

A spokesperson for Shell confirmed that a search for new investors or even buyers was included in the reorganization plan.

Earlier this month, Reuters reported, citing sources, that Ometto was still deciding the matter but unlikely to commit additional funds under current macroeconomic conditions.

Ometto praised the nomination of Bradesco's chairman Luiz Carlos Trabuco to the Finance Ministry on Thursday, saying the appointment would benefit Brazil's economy.

"This was fantastic, he is a finance expert and a person of absolute integrity," Ometto said.

($1 = 5.54 Brazilian reais)

data.title: RBI allows White Label ATM operators to source cash from multiple banks, buy directly from central bank
data.description:
The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) on November 27 allowed White Label ATM Operators (WLAOs) to source cash from multiple banks, including cooperative banks and regional rural banks, instead of relying solely on their sponsor banks. Operators can also purchase wholesale cash directly from the central bank, subject to a minimum threshold.

Under the new Master Directions on White Label ATM Operators, WLAOs can tie up with their sponsor banks as well as other scheduled banks for cash supply. The move gives operators greater flexibility in managing cash availability at their ATMs.

The directions state that WLAOs may tie up with “any other scheduled banks, including Cooperative Banks and Regional Rural Banks for cash supply at WLAs delinking cash supply from that of only sponsor bank arrangements”.

While the cash will be owned by the WLAO, the bank supplying it will be responsible for ensuring the “quality and genuineness of cash loaded” into the ATMs. Operators and cash-supplying banks may enter into service-level agreements to ensure an adequate supply of genuine and good-quality currency notes.

Operators can buy cash directly from RBI

The RBI has also permitted WLAOs to purchase wholesale cash directly from its issue offices and currency chests, provided the purchase exceeds one lakh pieces of any denomination and is made in multiples of that threshold.

The directions state that WLAOs “may buy wholesale cash, above a threshold of 1 lakh pieces (and in multiples thereof) of any denomination, directly from the Reserve Bank (Issue Offices) and Currency Chests against full payment”.

Operators can approach the respective issue departments of RBI regional offices with a list of their ATM locations to establish links with currency chests.

Multiple sponsor banks, wider ATM services

WLAOs can now have more than one sponsor bank, with transactions serviced by each sponsor bank settled through it. A sponsor bank must be a member of an RBI-authorised ATM or card payment network operator and the real-time gross settlement (RTGS) system.

The RBI has also permitted WLAOs to offer bill payment and interoperable cash deposit services, subject to technical feasibility and certification by the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI).

They may also provide interoperable cardless cash withdrawals (ICCW) at their ATMs. The directions state that “UPI would be used for customer authorisation in such transactions”, while settlement would take place through the National Financial Switch or ATM networks.

WLA operators must also accept domestic and international cards issued under authorised card payment network schemes, including credit, debit and prepaid cards. They can offer dynamic currency conversion to international cardholders, with the conversion rate sourced from an authorised dealer bank.

Rural and semi-urban deployment remains mandatory

The RBI has retained the requirement for WLA operators to deploy a higher proportion of their ATMs in semi-urban and rural areas to expand access to banking services.

Their deployment pattern must maintain a minimum ratio of 1:2:3 across metro, urban, semi-urban and rural regions, respectively, with the requirement reviewed by the RBI at least once every six months. WLAOs are also not permitted to take over ATMs operated by banks.

Non-bank entities seeking authorisation to operate WLAs must maintain a minimum net worth of Rs 100 crore at all times, based on their latest audited balance sheet.

Issuing banks responsible for failed transaction complaints

The directions place primary responsibility for resolving customer complaints relating to failed transactions at WLAs on the issuing bank. The sponsor bank must provide the necessary support and ensure that the WLAO shares relevant records and information with the issuing bank.

The RBI said the existing timelines for resolving complaints and compensation for failed ATM transactions at bank-operated ATMs would also apply to WLAs.

If delays attributable to the sponsor bank or WLAO result in the issuing bank paying compensation to a customer, the issuing bank must be compensated by the sponsor bank. The sponsor bank can enter into agreements with the WLAO to recover the amount.

The directions, effective immediately, consolidate the existing framework and repeal 11 earlier circulars and guidelines issued between 2012 and January 2026.
